record.paper_title: A collection of open problems in celebration of Imre Leader’s 60th birthday
record.original_question: In the same equal-sized red-blue colorings of the k-dimensional discrete torus T_n^k, what are the possible analogous probability pairs for t-step random walks when t ≥ 3? In particular, even for k = 2, what is the correct description of these pairs?

evidence.quote: Another interesting generalisation is to consider the corresponding pairs of probabilities for t-step walks with t ≥ 3. Here, even the k = 2 case is open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k \geq 2$ and $n \geq 2$ be integers, and consider the $k$-dimensional discrete torus $T_n^k = (\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^k$, regarded as the Cayley graph in which each vertex $x$ is adjacent to the $2k$ vertices $x \pm e_i$ ($i = 1, \dots, k$), where $e_1, \dots, e_k$ is the standard basis. An equal-sized red-blue coloring of $T_n^k$ is a partition of its vertex set into two classes $R$ (red) and $B$ (blue) of equal size (assume $n^k$ is even).

For a fixed integer $t \geq 1$, let $(X_0, X_1, \dots, X_t)$ denote the simple random walk on $T_n^k$ of length $t$ with $X_0$ chosen uniformly at random from $T_n^k$ and each subsequent step uniformly chosen among the $2k$ neighbors. Given an equal-sized red-blue coloring $c : T_n^k \to \{R, B\}$, define
$$p_R(c, t) = \Pr[c(X_0) = R \text{ and } c(X_t) = R], \qquad p_B(c, t) = \Pr[c(X_0) = B \text{ and } c(X_t) = B].$$

Determine, for $t \geq 3$, the set of all pairs $(p_R, p_B) \in [0,1]^2$ that arise as $(p_R(c, t), p_B(c, t))$ for some $n$ and some equal-sized red-blue coloring $c$ of $T_n^k$. In particular, give a complete description of this set of attainable pairs in the case $k = 2$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as open in a collection of open problems, including the planar case k = 2. A targeted web search did not find any subsequent paper resolving the t ≥ 3 case for equal-sized red-blue colorings of the discrete torus, so the problem appears still open.
